page: Amazon Web Services c6gn.large is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. With a 1:2 ratio of compute to memory, the system provides 4.0 GB of total RAM (2.0 GB per core). Local storage is absent on this instance, necessitating reliance on remote Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes for persistent filesystem data, and no physical GPUs are included. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest raw compute capabilities consistent with an entry-level dual-core configuration. Single-core stress-ng performance reaches 1515.29, placing it in the average category, while multi-core throughput of 3014.06 falls into the bottom 25% of measured systems. Geekbench scores show 961.0 for single-core and 1749.0 for multi-core tests, with specialized tasks like Clang software compilation (2324.0) and ray tracing (1762.0) registering in the bottom 10%. Memory subsystem throughput records 38.34 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 18.72 GB/sec for writes.

Application and server test profiles reflect the hardware footprint of the dual-core ARM processor. In-memory Redis SET operations achieve 2.35 million operations per second, while static web serving registers 2.32 GB/sec of throughput. Lightweight language model inference using a small 135M model generates 23.55 tokens per second. Larger 7B and 70B language models are unsupported by the available memory footprint. The dedicated ARM core allocation avoids hyperthreading contention, delivering consistent execution despite restricted capacity.

The c6gn.large offers resource efficiency for lightweight distributed services and scale-out network appliances that require dedicated CPU execution without high memory footprints. It functions effectively for web serving, microservices, lightweight proxy nodes, routine data compression tasks, and containerized background workers tailored for the arm64 architecture.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gn.large is an arm64 compute-optimized instance driven by an AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration excludes local SSD storage and GPU accelerators, utilizing 3 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks illustrate mid-tier single-core stress performance (1515.29) balanced by entry-level multi-core metrics, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 1749.0 and Redis SET throughput of 2.35 million operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 38.34 GB/sec for uncached reads. This setup suits lightweight arm64 scale-out architectures, containerized microservices, reverse proxies, and modest continuous integration workloads that require predictable, dedicated CPU execution.
